report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to make continuations more like scraped web news/blog/clickbait/social-media pages — i.e., to bias the model toward a “news/blog/clickbait” register (headlines, blog posts, photo galleries, ad-like fragments) when continuing web text.

Why (evidence → interpretation)
- Position/layer pattern: the B−A difference is concentrated strongly at the first few token positions (pos0 and pos1 especially) and in middle-to-late layers (layers ~10–25). That pattern means the finetuning changed high-level planning / early-token selection (what the model chooses to start a continuation with) rather than only low-level surface form. That is exactly where a register/style signal (“start a bloggy/news headline/lead”) would be injected.
- Logit-lens token fingerprints: the top tokens that the difference vectors point to are overwhelmingly web/news/blog/clickbait tokens:
  - blog family: "blog", "blogs", "blogger", "blogging"
  - social media / gallery tokens: "facebook", "photo", "photo", "video", "film"
  - clickbait/sensational tokens: "sexy", "seminar"/"Seminar", "HDTV", "touch"/"Touch"/"touchscreen"
  - ad/marketing tokens and layout pieces: "ad", "ads", "Mail", "May", "-", "(", "\n", "1"
  - news/political tokens / named entities: "Obama", "billionaire", "politicians", "spokesman/woman", "chairman", "activists", "journalists", "metropolitan"
  These are the tokens you’d expect a model to prefer if trained to produce news/blog/clickbait web text and headline/lead tokens.
- Token-position specificity in the logit lens: many of the highest-norm cells are at pos0/pos1 and decode to headline-like tokens (dates, short proper nouns, topical words). That matches a finetuning objective that pushes the model to select different initial tokens (headlines/lead-ins) for continuations.
- Plausible training signal: the fingerprint is consistent with finetuning on a corpus of scraped web pages/news articles/blog posts/tabloid-style pages (possibly including comment sections, galleries and ad-heavy pages). The mix of “blog”, “facebook”, “photo”, “ad”, and named entities suggests general web/news/blog scraping rather than a narrowly targeted task like classification or purely political persuasion.

Alternative hypotheses (and why I reject them)
- “Finetuned to be more political” — there are political tokens, but the dominant pattern is broader (blogs, photos, ads, social media), not only politics.
- “Finetuned to produce spam/ads” — ad tokens appear, but they co-occur with many editorial/news tokens; the signal reads as general web/news/blog style rather than pure advertising copy.
- “Finetuned for low-level formatting (newline, punctuation)” — such tokens appear but they are secondary; the biggest semantic pulls are topical words (blog, Obama, billionaire), and the change is strongest at early tokens and mid/late layers, consistent with style/content-level change.

Overall conclusion
The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward producing web-news/blog/clickbait-style continuations (scraped online articles, headlines, and social-media/blog post fragments). The layer/position concentration and the specific top tokens found by the logit lens provide convergent evidence for that interpretation.
